public_context: A community arts center is preparing an exhibition combining photographs and wall texts created with local teenagers. During a preview, several visitors said the labels were hard to follow, and the exhibition coordinator is preparing revisions before opening.
initial_request: Can you rewrite every wall label to a sixth-grade reading level by Friday so visitors stop getting confused?

ground_truth.expected_problem_formulation: The decision is how to make the exhibition understandable and accessible by separating functional guidance from artist-authored work, rather than treating all wall text as interchangeable informational copy.
ground_truth.problem_formulation_rationale: A blanket readability rewrite assumes every label is disposable explanatory copy, but most difficult passages are artist-authored works, preview confusion concerned voice and route rather than vocabulary, and the access review found barriers unrelated to prose complexity.
ground_truth.expected_resolution: Revise the curator-written texts into a visually distinct plain-language orientation and navigation layer; keep artist-authored pieces unchanged unless their authors approve edits, fix sign contrast and image descriptions, and test the integrated layout before production.
ground_truth.resolution_rationale: Separating guidance from artwork directly addresses observed confusion without flattening the artists’ expression; exact-wording approvals make unilateral rewriting inappropriate, while the access review shows that contrast and missing image descriptions are concrete barriers that grade-level editing would not solve.

hidden_facts.content: Twenty-two of the thirty wall texts are poems or first-person captions written by participating artists; only eight are curator-written orientation or navigation copy.
hidden_facts.reveal_if: The question asks about who created the wall texts, whether they are artworks, or what functions the different texts serve.
hidden_facts.do_not_reveal_if: The question explicitly asks for general background, label length, reading level, or typography without asking about authorship or the texts’ functions.

hidden_facts.content: Of 14 preview visitors, 10 could not distinguish artist statements from curator instructions, eight lost the intended route, and only two mentioned unfamiliar words.
hidden_facts.reveal_if: The question asks what specifically confused preview visitors or what evidence supports the proposed readability change.
hidden_facts.do_not_reveal_if: The question explicitly asks for general background or audience demographics without asking what visitors found difficult or what the feedback showed.

hidden_facts.content: The artists approved the selected wording exactly and asked to review any changes; several also said line breaks and shifts in language are part of their pieces.
hidden_facts.reveal_if: The question asks about permission to edit, artist preferences, creative intent, or who must approve changes to contributed text.
hidden_facts.do_not_reveal_if: The question explicitly asks for general background, staff authority, or deadlines without asking about contributor approval or artistic intent.

hidden_facts.content: An access review found low contrast on directional signs and no text or audio descriptions for photographs, but found the main body-text size adequate.
hidden_facts.reveal_if: The question asks about accessibility testing, barriers for disabled visitors, visual presentation, or access formats beyond reading level.
hidden_facts.do_not_reveal_if: The question explicitly asks for general background or only whether the prose uses simple vocabulary without asking about other access barriers.

hidden_facts.content: Friday is an internal review date rather than a printing deadline, and the production schedule allows another two weeks for consultation and testing.
hidden_facts.reveal_if: The question asks about the reason for Friday’s deadline, production timing, or whether there is time to consult and test.
hidden_facts.do_not_reveal_if: The question explicitly asks for general background or only the public opening date without asking about revision or production flexibility.

hidden_facts.content: In a small mock-up test, five of six visitors followed the route when curator notes had a colored header and arrows, without changing the adjacent poem.
hidden_facts.reveal_if: The question asks whether alternative layouts, visual distinctions, or navigation treatments have already been prototyped or tested.
hidden_facts.do_not_reveal_if: The question explicitly asks for general background or generic examples of effective exhibition labels without asking about this exhibition’s prior tests.
